GoPi merger — the branch-merge DAEMON (a resident server-side service).

TOP-LEVEL BECAUSE IT IS A SERVICE: the merger is an independent resident
process, the peer of 'gopi worker'. It claims no tasks and runs no tasks —
it merges branches. 'gopi worker' (which claims and runs tasks) is top-level
for the same reason: both are process forms a host starts from its own
service unit; neither is a ledger verb.

One pass (the six-sweep merge surface):
  adoption → merged-branch cleanup → branch scan → git-sync →
  merge-backlog audit → merge-backlog executor
then the post-merge REBUILD of every configured repo whose pass landed work
(GOPI.md Rule 12: merge → cleanup → rebuild).

Usage:
  gopi merger                    # FOREGROUND resident daemon (Ctrl+C to stop)
  gopi merger --daemon           # detach to the background, return at once
  gopi merger --once             # one pass, then exit 0 (the E2E seam)
  gopi merger --every 30s        # poll period (Go duration: 30s, 5m, 1h)
  gopi merger --status           # READ-ONLY: is it running, what would it merge
  gopi merger --stop             # GRACEFUL stop: finish the in-flight pass,
                                 #   release the lock, exit 0
  gopi merger --restart          # --stop, then start a fresh daemon (picks up
                                 #   the current binary — the restart idiom)
  gopi merger --start            # start a daemon only if none is running
  gopi merger -h | --help        # this help — starts NOTHING (zero side-effects)

Flags:
  --every DURATION   poll period between passes (default 5m)
  --once             single pass, then exit 0
  --daemon           detach: start a background daemon and return immediately
  --db PATH          task ledger override (conflict dispatch + resolve rows)
  --no-branch-scan   skip the unmerged-branch inventory pass
  --stop             graceful stop of the running merger (see below)
  --restart          --stop (bounded wait) then start a fresh daemon
  --start            start a daemon only when none is running
  --force            INTERRUPT in-flight work (with --stop/--restart): the
                     merger reports what it cut, kills its in-flight children,
                     restores every configured repo to a buildable tip, and
                     fires the "merger-forced-exit" notify event
  --wait DURATION    bound on the graceful wait (default 25m; 0 = do not wait)

Restart / graceful stop (why the default never interrupts):
  A merger pass owns the integration branch, and a pass may be blocked on a
  resolve or verify CHILD working in its own worktree. So a stop request is
  honoured at PASS BOUNDARIES only: the merger finishes the pass it is in
  (including waiting for its children), then exits and releases the
  single-instance lock. Nothing is unlinked or re-acquired on the way out, so
  the very next 'gopi merger' takes the lock immediately.
  Delivery is belt-and-braces: a durable per-instance request file under
  <gopi data root>/merger (TERM_<pid> / FORCE_<pid>) PLUS a signal — SIGTERM
  (also SIGINT/SIGUSR1) means "finish, then exit"; SIGUSR2 means "interrupt
  now". The file alone is enough when signals cannot be delivered; the signal
  alone is enough when the file cannot be written.
  --force is the ONLY path that interrupts work, and it repays it: it prints
  what it interrupted (pass start, repo/branch, child pids), kills those
  children, and returns every configured repo to its buildable tip (an
  unfinished merge is aborted, never left for the next merger to trip over).
  Exit codes: 0 = the requested end state holds; 1 = it does not (still busy
  past --wait, an ambiguous live set, a failed start).
  The operator's post-update flow (devdoc/merger-graceful-restart-20260912.md):
      gopi merger --restart          # stop gracefully, then run the new binary
      gopi merger --stop --force     # only when a graceful stop will not finish

--daemon (the flag that replaces an external setsid/nohup/& launch):
  the daemon takes the single-instance lock FIRST — in the process you are
  waiting on — hands it to a detached child, and returns only after that
  child has PROVEN it is running (a pipe handshake). So the exit status is
  a real answer, not a guess:
    exit 0  → the daemon is up; stdout names its pid and its log file
    exit ≠0 → the daemon did NOT start; stderr says why (including a
              single-instance refusal naming the pid that holds the lock)
  The child is a session leader (setsid) with stdin closed, so it survives
  your shell. Its stdout+stderr go to:
    <gopi data root>/logs/merger.log          (default ~/.gopi/logs/merger.log)

Single instance:
  flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on <gopi data root>/serve.lock — a second merger (or
  a second --daemon start while one runs) is REFUSED rather than silently
  double-merging. The lock is inherited across the fork, so the guarantee
  holds for a detached daemon exactly as for a foreground one.

Privileges (--daemon):
  A detached merger needs NO privilege: start it as the ordinary user you
  already are. Running it as root does not obtain the escape either — a
  process inherits its cgroup from its launcher, so a privileged daemon was
  measured in the SAME login session scope as its unprivileged launcher, and
  root has no user manager of its own to migrate into (both measured).
  When the escape is unavailable the start says so and the daemon runs
  anyway: setsid already removes the controlling-terminal exposure, and what
  remains is that it ends with the session scope. --require-scope turns that
  degradation into a refused start when you need the guarantee rather than
  the convenience. For a start that outlives the login session, a host's own
  service unit is the operator's lever — not a password.
  NO privilege is needed by '--once', or by a FOREGROUND 'gopi merger': they
  run in your session's scope by DESIGN (Ctrl+C / the session ends them),
  detach nothing, and touch no cgroup — so the privilege question does not
  arise there either.

Sweep targets:
  the settings.json "repos" table keys (one key per repo; an entry with an
  empty build is a valid PURE merge target). No --repo flag, no cwd
  assumption: configure the sweep list in settings.json.

Deprecated aliases (still accepted for running deployments):
  gopi task merger …   # the daemon's pre-promotion home (foreground only)
  gopi task serve …    # the daemon's pre-split name
